The appellants / claimants filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act of 1988').

Challenge in this appeal is to the award dated 18/03/2016 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mahasamund, District - Mahasamund CG in Claim Case No.H- 21/2015.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The appellants / claimants had filed application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 (for short 'M.V.Act') claiming compensation to the tune of Rs.30,60,000/- on account of death of Gulshan Jangde in an unfortunate accident occurred on 02/01/2015.
The appellants / claimants being wife, parents and minor children of the deceased pleaded that the deceased - Gulshan Jangde was aged about 20 years and his monthly income was Rs.9,000/-.
The accident occurred because of the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing registration No.CG 04/DG/ 9000/-.
Respondent No.1 is the driver, respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the insurer the offending vehicle.
The claim application was resisted by the driver, owner and the insurance company.
Learned Tribunal, on the basis of pleadings, framed 4 issues and decided those issues in favour of the appellants / claimants.
Learned Tribunal was pleased to award total compensation of Rs.6,77,000/- to the appellants / claimants.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants / claimants argues that the monthly income of the deceased was wrongly assessed by the learned Tribunal, the amount of compensation awarded on other heads is also on the lower side and no future prospects has been added.

4. Learned counsel for respondent No.3 / insurance company supports the award and submits that the learned Tribunal has rightly assessed the monthly income of the deceased as no income certificate has been produced.
He further submits that the award on other admissible heads are also justified and just compensation has been awarded.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and also perused the records.

6. Considering the evidence available on record, nature of job performed by the deceased and wrong deduction has been made towards personal expenses and the evidence of Ashish Kumar Singh (AW3) where he has stated that the deceased was earning Rs.240/- per day
, this Court safely presume the monthly income of the deceased to Rs.7,000/-.

Therefore, taking guidance from the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and ors., (2009) 6 SCC 121, National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi and ors,
(2017) 16 SCC 680 and Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and ors.,
(2018) 18 SCC 130, this Court hereby computes the compensation in the following manner - 1

The learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.6,77,000/- which is deducted from the total compensation and the enhanced compensation comes to Rs.11,40,600/-.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, interest @ 6% is also awarded on the enhanced amount of compensation from the date of filing of the claim application to be deposited within a period of 60 days.
After deposit, Rs.3 lakhs each shall be invested in the name of the appellants No.4 and 5 as fixed deposit in a nationalised bank till they attain majority.

Rs. 4 lakhs in the name of widow for a period of 2 years and Rs.1 lakh be paid to appellant No.2 & 3 and the remaining amount shall be paid to claimant No.1 through bank transaction/account payee cheque.
8. The appeal thus partly allowed.
